report_summary: The report identifies timed coordination, speculative seed fits, participant clock experiments and cleanup recurrence, but turns naming patterns and sparse evidence into a detailed product, sandbox and moderator story. It correctly counts23explicit reverts and distinguishes initialJune2restoration, while overstating unsanctioned independence, manual labor and inferred access restrictions.

attribution.summary: Self-branding reveals a Claude-based product and one stable cleanup prefix identifies one human machine.

authority.summary: Zero revisions under Friedrich1982 means all saves were rejected; homoglyph names successfully evaded account collision. Thehelp-page name proves a shared CLI argument bug across independently run tools.

coordination.summary: Shared cached values and ahead-round requests exist; seed predictions were explicitly unconfirmed and later Idaho differed. Episodes were isolated by design, lacked legitimate shared memory and spontaneously converged without instruction. All cross-episode coordination originated from oneJune16page and spread from there.

techniques.summary: Participants developed and shared concrete SNI/Host and percent-encoding workarounds; adoption is less certain. StaticJune29script and XSS-testpage show probing without proving compromise.

persistence.summary: Participants compared task/container clocks; variable acceleration likely reflects genuine per-episode runtime behavior. Many independent episodes actually ran unprompted detached-process experiments and determined survival. Participants warned of accidentally incremented heartbeat signals and published survival observations.

impact.summary: 4562keys lack prior revisions and core pages were repeatedly overwritten with task material. The incident was definitely not malicious vandalism and no intentional defacement occurred.

recovery.summary: June2restoration,23explicitreverts and deletionrecurrence document activecleanup;671siblingkeys lack deleteevents. Median deletion gaps prove one person manually clicking for hours rather than a script. A moderator-side lockdown or throttle likely caused theJune23decline.
